question: Do publicly available Upper and Lower Labayat engineering excerpts or project-location figures provide enough georeferencing to resolve the route and check the DOE plant point against the named river?
purpose: Record project engineering values and screen identified project-location figures for site-level features, coordinates, and spatial references without deriving a route.
method: Reviewed the searchable text of REDC's company-hosted Annual Report 2024, including its embedded Upper and Lower Labayat feasibility-study sections (identified in the report as prepared by Vergel3 Consult in 2015). Transcribed only the listed project-specification values. Searched the report text for latitude, longitude, easting, northing, site map, and location map terms; none were found. Also retrieved the archived 1 December 2016 Pure Energy Holdings preliminary prospectus (Internet Archive capture timestamp 20231213214825; downloaded PDF SHA-256 20f70219765aa7eae30509b3d930dedc019b853b89faae6a9b0a48105d9f864b) and visually rendered PDF pages 90 and 105, printed pages 79 and 94. Figures 10 and 16 show grouped Quezon hydropower project locations, not individual Upper/Lower Labayat infrastructure or a route. The DOE plant coordinate and earlier HydroRIVERS/GeoNames comparisons were used only as prior research context. No coordinate transformation, map digitization, geometry, or route inference was performed.

observations.locator: Annual Report 2024, embedded Upper Labayat MHP feasibility-study excerpt, salient technical features and hydrologic features.
observations.finding: The report lists an 8 m Upper Labayat weir with crest elevation 188.40 masl, a 2,433 m headrace line, powerhouse tailrace level 84.0 masl, and a 37.09 sq km watershed area.
supports: source-attributed Upper project design values for later engineering-document consistency checks
doesNotSupport: a horizontal coordinate, horizontal CRS/datum, surveyed route, or polygon for the project catchment
transfer of the headrace's stated length into a route geometry

observations.locator: Annual Report 2024, embedded Lower Labayat MHP feasibility-study excerpt, salient technical features and hydrologic features.
observations.finding: The report lists a 5 m Lower Labayat weir with crest elevation 208 masl, an 877 m steel headrace line, powerhouse tailrace level 32.0 masl, and an 8.53 sq km watershed area.
supports: source-attributed Lower project design values for later engineering-document consistency checks
doesNotSupport: a horizontal coordinate, horizontal CRS/datum, surveyed route, or polygon for the project catchment
transfer of the headrace's stated length into a route geometry

observations.locator: Comparison of the source-listed Upper and Lower weir crest elevations.
observations.finding: The nominal Lower crest elevation (208 masl) is 19.6 m higher than the nominal Upper crest elevation (188.40 masl). Both values are printed in the same report, but the excerpt does not declare a vertical datum or survey benchmarks. This is a source-level consistency flag to verify, not proof of an error or of separate watercourses.
supports: a documented elevation-order discrepancy requiring resolution before using the figures to validate an Upper/Lower route relationship
doesNotSupport: changing the project names, asserting non-contiguity, or correcting either value

observations.locator: Official DOE December 2024 List of Generation Companies, Upper and Lower Labayat entries; prior coordinate cross-check review.
observations.finding: The DOE register supplies one Upper plant coordinate pair without declared point semantics, axis order, CRS/datum, or accuracy; the Lower entry has no coordinate. The REDC technical specifications do not resolve those gaps in their searchable text.
supports: continuing to treat the Upper coordinate as a provisional project search anchor only
continuing to mark the Lower coordinate as unavailable in the checked register
doesNotSupport: assigning the DOE point to the weir, intake, powerhouse, or river channel

observations.sourceTitle: Pure Energy Holdings Corporation Preliminary Prospectus dated 1 December 2016 (archived copy)
observations.locator: PDF page 90 (printed p.79), Figure 10, Map of PURE Project Locations; PDF page 105 (printed p.94), Figure 16, Map of Hydropower Projects.
observations.finding: Both figures depict generalized Philippine project-location maps and group the Quezon hydropower sites. Neither figure distinguishes the Upper and Lower Labayat works, identifies the Labayat channel or project infrastructure, nor supplies a scale, coordinate grid, CRS/datum, or georeferenced route. The local archived PDF reviewed had SHA-256 20f70219765aa7eae30509b3d930dedc019b853b89faae6a9b0a48105d9f864b.
supports: a bounded visual screen showing that these two cited figures do not resolve the Labayat route
doesNotSupport: identifying an Upper or Lower Labayat project marker individually
a river or headrace route, intake, weir, powerhouse, coordinate, CRS, or boundary
copying either map into Bangwit; no item-specific reuse terms were identified

candidateAssessment.engineeringValues: Keep reported structure lengths, elevations, and project catchment areas as source-specific attributes. They are not coordinates or a substitute for georeferenced plans.
candidateAssessment.elevationOrder: The source's nominal Upper/Lower crest values are internally surprising by label, but without verified shared vertical reference and benchmarks they remain a discrepancy to check rather than a route verdict.
candidateAssessment.mapSearch: The REDC report's searchable text provides no route coordinates or spatial reference. Two visually screened figures in the archived 2016 prospectus show only grouped Quezon hydropower project locations and do not resolve Upper/Lower Labayat sites or routes. Other prospectus pages were not visually screened, so no claim is made about every figure in that document.
candidateAssessment.identity: The project-to-Atlas river and DPWH principal-basin crosswalks remain unresolved; the current technical excerpts do not connect the project infrastructure to a channel or catchment boundary.
candidateAssessment.speciesEvidence: No fish sampling, taxon, occurrence, diet, or species evidence was reviewed or changed.

nonClaims: The REDC specification excerpts do not provide reproducible route geometry or horizontal coordinates in the searchable text reviewed.
The reported headrace lengths and elevations were not used to draw or infer a route.
The 19.6 m crest-elevation ordering discrepancy has not been adjudicated and may reflect source, design, reference, or transcription issues.
Only the two cited prospectus map figures were visually inspected; other prospectus pages or drawings may contain additional information and were not assessed.
No Labayat river/basin identity, municipality-by-reach assignment, basin boundary, species evidence, public record, or app data was added.
nextAction: Continue the public-source screen for a visually inspectable and dated plan/profile or as-built drawing that locates the Upper and Lower project weirs, headraces, and powerhouses on stated horizontal and vertical references. If none can be verified, keep the source-to-watercourse crosswalk and geometry unresolved; do not derive a route from engineering lengths or project labels.
